title: carex latebrosa
intro: Carex latebrosa, commonly known as the "late-brooding sedge," is a type of plant species in the family Cyperaceae. It is a perennial herb native to the mountainous regions of Asia, known for its medicinal properties. The plant has been traditionally used for its health benefits, which include anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and antioxidant activities, as well as its ability to aid in respiratory issues and skin conditions. The bioactive constituents of Carex latebrosa include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and terpenoids, which are responsible for its therapeutic actions, including its sedative, antispasmodic, and anti-inflammatory effects.
